asked_by: operator 10/15: no-progress cut was turned off live at 11:25; test what is best, including the no-progress cut gated by the double check (sell only if both %R lines are falling)
engine: tools/replay_session.py (live code), whole config pinned to the commit the sweep runs at; only the exit-cut knobs vary. Double check reads only the replay-fed point-in-time ob_observe bars (never the live fetch, which has no end time).

arms.off: no-progress off, double check off (live since 10/15 11:25)
arms.dc180: double check alone at 180 s (under entry, both %R lines down)
arms.np_dc: no-progress 180 s, sells only when the double check says both lines down (operator's proposal)

metric: VALUE = sum of net bp per day (net = return minus full SIP spread at entry), day-clustered, paired vs off; also net bp per trade, opens, hold.
decision: Ship the arm with the highest mean daily VALUE if it beats 'off' in BOTH halves and its paired t vs off is >= 1.5 (8 days; this is a config choice on paper, not an edge claim). If no arm qualifies, keep 'off'. Ties within 2 bp/day go to the arm that holds longer (operator preference to keep positions open).
caveats: 8 days; in-sample for nothing (no arm was tuned on these days)
replay recall vs live is ~0.5-0.6, so absolute values differ from live; the comparison is between arms on the same replayed opens
exits cannot move the mean (42 shapes ~0 gross): expect differences of a few bp
